AZUSA AUDITORIUM
213 EAST FOOTHILL BOULEVARD

1.

2.
Roll Call
CEREMONIAL
1.
Councilmember Macias: Presentation of a check to Post 16 from, Los Angeles County Fire Station 32 in Azusa.
CLOSED SESSION
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR CLOSED SESSION
Prior to going into closed session the City Council will convene in the Auditorium serving as Council Chambers to take public comment on the closed session items only. General public comment will be provided for during the regular portion of the meeting beginning at 7:30 P.M.
1.
CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54957.6. City Negotiators: Troy L. Butzlaff, City Manager and Theresa St. Peter, Interim Human Resources Director
Organizations: ACEA (Azusa City Employee Association), CAPP (Civilian Association of Police Personnel), AMMA (Azusa Middle Management Association).
2.
CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION - Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1). Rocky Wenrick vs. City of Azusa, Request for Settlement Authority, Workers Compensation Appeals Board Numbers ADJ3533323, ADJ835061, ADJ4346973 and ADJ3996538.
3.
CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - POTENTIAL LITIGATION - Pursuant to California Government Code Sections 54956.9(d)(2)/54956.9(e)(2). 2 Potential Cases.
4.
CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION - Pursuant to   California Government Code, Section 54956.9(d)(2).      1 Potential Case. (Claim filed by Azusa Unified School District related to Rosedale Development School Mitigation)
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are in file on the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are in the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.ci.azusa.ca.us. Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. Cards submitted after 7:30 P.M. will not be accepted.
7:30 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
A.
PRELIMINARY BUSINESS
1.
Call to Order
2.
Roll Call
3.
Pledge to the Flag - Mr. Dominic Chavira.
4.
Invocation - Pastor Rick McDonald, Azusa House of Prayer.
B.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the council/agency board that are not listed on this agenda or are listed on this agenda as an item other than a public hearing item. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the city council/agency board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the council/agency board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. The council/agency board will respond after public comment has been received. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments shall be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.
C.
REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL
1.
Update on the Intermodal Parking Structure.
C-1 Update on Intermodal Parking Structure
2.
Update and presentation regarding Azusa Rock/Vulcan mining operations and reclamation efforts.
3.
Councilmember Gonzales: Discussion regarding the creation of a Welcoming Committee, for the 2015 Los Angeles Special Olympics Athletes from South Africa visiting Azusa.
4.
Councilmember Gonzales: Request for certificates for Azusa Pacific University NCAA Baskeball Team, to be presented at the Council Meeting of April 20, 2015.
5.
Mayor Rocha: Request for Certificates of recognition for Misses Alicia Ayala and Rosie Herrera, Azusa residents who were selected by Congresswoman Grace Napolitano for the 32nd Congressional District Women of the Year "Unsung Heroines" Award, to be presented April 10, 2015.
C-5 Certificates Unsung Heroines
6.
Recreation and Family Services Department: Request for a proclamation, proclaiming Arbor Day in Azusa, to be presented April 16, 2015, 5:00 P.M. at Memorial Park.
D.
SCHEDULED ITEMS
1.
PUBLIC HEARING - RESOLUTION TO VACATE AND ABANDON A PORTION OF ALAMEDA AVENUE.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Open the Public Hearing, receive testimony, close the Public Hearing and adopt Resolution No. 2015-C15, titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Azusa Ordering the Vacation of a Portion of Alameda Avenue In The City of Azusa". This project is exempt from any additional review of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) based on Pub. Res. Code § 21166; State CEQA Guidelines § 15162.
D-1 Public Hearing - Vacate Portion of Alameda Ave
2.
ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION APPROVING THE GENERAL FUND RESERVE BALANCE POLICY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2015-C16, adopting and approving a General Fund Reserve Policy.
D-2 Resolution General Fund Reserve Policy
3.
ASSIGNMENTS OF OUTSIDE AGENCIES BOARDS AND COMMITTEES.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Council may choose to ratify the existing assignments of outside agencies Boards and Committees for an additional two year period from April 2015 to March 2017; or re-assign the existing assignments as Council deems necessary.
D-3 Assignment Outside Agencies Boards and Committees
4.
CONSIDERATION OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JOE A. GONSALVES & SONS FOR LEGISLATIVE ADVOCACY SERVICES
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Waive the competitive purchasing requirement per Azusa Municipal Code Section 2-523 (b), approve a Professional Services Agreement with Joe A. Gonsalves & Sons in an amount not to exceed $4,000 per month, for legislative advocacy services through June 30, 2015, and authorize the City Manager to execute, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, a professional services agreement with Joe A. Gonsalves & Sons for legislative advocacy services in an amount not-to-exceed $4,000 per month.
D-4 Joe Gonsalves Legislative Advocacy Letter Agreement
D-4 Joe Gonsalves Legislative Advocacy Letter Agreement
E.
CONSENT CALENDAR
The Consent Calendar adopting the printed recommended actions will be enacted with one vote. If Councilmembers or Staff wish to address any item on the Consent Calendar
individually, it will be considered under SPECIAL CALL ITEMS.
1.
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETINGS OF MARCH 2 AND MARCH 16, 2015 AND THE SPECIAL MEETINGS OF FEBRUARY 23 AND MARCH 23, 2015.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the minutes as written.
E-1 Minutes, February 23, 2015, Special Meeting
E-1 Minutes, March 2, 2015
E-1 Minutes, March 16, 2015 Special-Regular Meeting
E-1 Minutes, March 23, 2015, Special Meeting
2.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENT OF WARRANTS BY THE CITY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2015-C17 allowing certain claims and demands and specifying the funds out of which the same are to be paid.
E-2 Resolution Warrant Register
3.
CONSIDERATION OF AMENDED AND RESTATED PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MORSE PLANNING GROUP.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the amended and restated Professional Services Agreement with Morse Planning Group, for project management services in an amount not-to-exceed $25,000.
E-3 Amended and Restated Agreement Morse Planning Group
4.
CONSIDERATION OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH CBRE, INC. TO PERFORM A RETAIL LEAKAGE AND SURPLUS ANALYSIS OF THE CITY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Waive the competitive purchasing requirement per Azusa Municipal Code Section 2-523 (b) and approve an agreement with CBRE, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $25,000, to perform a retail leakage and surplus analysis of the City, and authorize the City Manager to execute, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, a Professional Services Agreement with CBRE.
E-4 CBRE Professional Services Agreement for Marketing Efforts
5.
REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS/PROPOSALS REGARDING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT LABOR COMPLIANCE (CDBG) PROFESSIONAL SERVICES.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the scope of work for CDBG labor compliance services, and authorize staff to issue a Request for Qualifications/Proposals for CDBG labor compliance professional services.
E-5 Request for Proposals CDBG Consultant Services
6.
LEASE OF 3 UNMARKED POLICE VEHICLES FROM ENTERPRISE FLEET SERVICES.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the leasing of three, unmarked police vehicles from Enterprise Fleet Services, Ontario, CA, in an amount not to exceed $13,455.24 annually, total cost of the 48 month lease will be $53,820.96, and authorize the City Manger to enter into a Lease Agreement with Enterprise Fleet Services.
E-6 Lease 3 Unmarked Police Vehicles
E-6 Attachment 1, Quote 2788567
E-6 Attachment 2, Quote 2788602
E-6 Attachment 3, Quote 2788671
E-6 Attachment 4, Sample Lease Agreement
7.
AZUSA SAFE ROUTES TO SCHOOL - PROJECT WALK AND ROLL NO. SRTSLNI-5112(015) - NOTICE OF COMPLETION.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve a Notice of Completion for the Safe Routes to School Project No. SRTSLNI-5112 (015); and authorize staff to file the Notice of Completion with the Los Angeles County Clerk.
E-7 Notice of Completion Safe Routes to School
8.
FINANCIAL ADVISORS TO EVALUATE AND FACILITATE REFUNDING OF: (i) WATER PARITY REVENUE BONDS SERIES 2006; (ii) ROSEDALE COMMUNITY FACILITIES DISTRICT 2007 SPECIAL TAX BOND; AND (iii) THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY TAX ALLOCATION BOND 2005 SERIES A.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the selection of Fieldman-Rolapp & Associates ("FRA") to serve as Financial Advisor for Water Parity Revenue Bonds Series 2006 in a not-to-exceed amount of $40,500; and approve the selection of Urban Futures, Inc. ("UFI") to serve as Financial Advisor for Rosedale Community Facilities District 2007 Special Tax Bond in a not-to-exceed amount of $58,000.
E-8 Selection of Financical Advisors
E-8 Exhibit A, Financial Advisor Water Parity
E-8 Exhibit B, Financial Advisor, Refund 2007 Rosedale CFD Bond
E-8 Exhibit C, Financial Advisor, Refund 2005 RDA TABs
9.
CITY TREASURER'S STATEMENT OF CASH AND INVESTMENT BALANCES FOR THE MONTH OF FEBRUARY 2015.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive, review and file the Treasurer's Report for the City of Azusa for the month of February 2015.
E-9 Treasurers Report as of February 2015
10.
ACCEPTANCE OF OAK HILL PARK IMPROVEMENTS AND PARKWAY LANDSCAPING IMPROVEMENTS ADJACENT TO A PORTION OF TRACT 66141 KNOWN AS THE SAGE COURT-GARDENIA NEIGHBORHOODS, IN THE ROSEDALE COMMUNITY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Accept the improvements of Oak Hill Park, and the parkway improvements adjacent to a portion of the Transit I, and Great Park II and III neighborhoods, also known as Sage Court and Gardenia, in the Rosedale Community, and approve an increase to the contract amount with ValleyCrest Landscape Maintenance in the amount of $9,480 annually for the maintenance of these improvements.
E-10 Oak Hill-Lyon Parkway Acceptance
11.
LICENSE AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY AND NET DEVELOPMENT CO, INC. FOR NET DEVELOPMENT CO, INC. TO ACCESS CERTAIN REAL PROPERTY OWNED BY THE CITY GENERALLY LOCATED AT 229 S. AZUSA AVE (APNS 8614-014-918; 8617-014-919; 8614-014-920) FOR THE LIMITED PURPOSE OF DEMOLISHING AND REMOVING THE EXISTING STRUCTURES ON THE PROPERTY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve the License Agreement, in substantially final form, with Net Development Co., Inc., to access the property located at 229 S. Azusa Avenue, for the demolition of the existing structure, and authorize the City Manager to execute the License Agreement on behalf of the City. This project is exempt from any additional review of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) based on Pub. Res. Code § 21166; State CEQA Guidelines § 15162.
E-11 DemolitionLicense Agreement for 229 S. Azusa
F.
SUCCESSOR AGENCY RELATED BUSINESS.
1.
RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING PAYMENT OF WARRANTS BY THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY.
RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. 2015-R5.
F-1 Resolution Warrant Register Successor Agency
G.
ADJOURNMENT
UPCOMING MEETINGS:
April 20, 2015, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting;
May 4, 2015, 6:30 p.m. Ceremonial/Closed Session, 7:30 p.m. Regular Meeting.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in a city meeting, please contact the City Clerk at 626-812-5229. Notification three (3) working days prior to the meeting when special services are needed will assist staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide access to the meeting.
